title: Hackers Use Fake Claude, ChatGPT and Copilot Installers to Spread Malware
content_md: Cybercriminals are using fake installers for popular artificial intelligence tools, including Claude , ChatGPT, and Microsoft Copilot, to infect victims with malware. The campaigns abuse user trust in well-known AI brands and often use malicious advertisements, poisoned search results, and fake download pages. Sophos X-Ops reviewed 12 months of Managed Detection and Response cases involving AI-related activity, covering July 2025 through June 2026. Of 86 initially tagged cases, researchers confirmed 34 as genuine malicious AI activity. Four additional cases found during investigations brought the total to 38. The main finding was clear: most attackers are not using advanced AI-driven malware. Instead, they are exploiting AI software as a lure. Thirty-five of the 38 confirmed cases involved malicious targeting of AI products, brands, or ecosystems. Fake AI software impersonation accounted for 30 cases. Claude was the most abused brand, appearing in 26 cases. Attackers created lookalike websites that claimed to offer Claude installers or AI coding tools. Victims commonly reached these pages through malicious search advertisements or typo-squatted domains that closely resembled real vendor websites. Malware-Laced Fake AI Installers Many campaigns used a social-engineering technique called InstallFix, a variation of ClickFix .
